## The question

Foundation models for time series are sold as a replacement for the feature
engineering that gradient-boosted trees need: no lags to design, no calendar to
encode, no per-series training. This series tests that claim on data where it is
hard to be right — the [M5 Forecasting --- Accuracy](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/m5-forecasting-accuracy)
panel, 30,490 item×store series of daily Walmart sales, 68% of days zero, a
median series selling 0.45 units a day, forecast 28 days ahead.

M5 was chosen for two specific reasons rather than its fame. Chronos-2 has **no
training leakage** on it, so a zero-shot number means something. And its
dynamics are mostly **endogenous**: on fev-bench the multivariate model beats
its univariate sibling by a hair (WQL 0.555 vs 0.559), which says the
cross-series machinery has little to feed on here. That makes it a clean test of
the model itself rather than of the covariates one can invent around it.

## What the three parts do

The order matters: each part exists because the previous one left a question open. The third
one ends without a verdict, and that is reported rather than smoothed over — the test it runs
disqualifies its own key instrument, which is more useful to know than a tidy conclusion
would have been.

::: {#series}
:::

## How to read the numbers

Three commitments, kept throughout, because they are what separates a benchmark
from a demonstration:

- **Every choice is made on a validation origin** (2016-03-27) and measured once
  on a test origin (2016-04-24). Nothing is selected on the window it is scored on.
- **The evaluation roster is frozen** before any model runs, and every metric is
  reported next to the number of series it was computed on.
- **Any two numbers whose difference is interpreted share their hardware.** CPU
  and GPU disagree in the third decimal of WQL, which is enough to invert a close
  ranking, so the Chronos-2 corpus is entirely GPU and every artifact carries the
  device it was produced on.

Code and artifacts: [`m5-chronos2`](https://github.com/amelien-quenet/m5-chronos2).
